note: Converse County park in a red-rock canyon around a natural bridge with LaPrele Creek still flowing beneath it, 11 mi W of Douglas (I-25 exit 151, then 5 mi S on County Road 13). A few first-come camping sites near the caretaker's house, where campers check in. No pets allowed in the park. The gate is locked overnight (8 pm to 8 am). --Claude
summary: County page: limited FCFS camping, open April - Oct 15, no pets, phone 307-358-3532. Camper reviews (2023-24): 8 free sites, check in at the caretaker's house, gate 8 pm-8 am. Creekside not supported: the camping loop by the caretaker's house sits ~30-40 m from LaPrele Creek behind a band of riparian trees and brush; recommend creekside -> not waterfront (reviewer's call). Pin OK.
flags: WATERFRONT: recommend 'creekside' -> 'not waterfront'. The sites are not numbered or mapped by the county; reviews put them across from the caretaker's house, which is the south loop (rigs on zoom-19 Esri at about 42.73403,-105.61282 and 42.73395,-105.61237). From there LaPrele Creek (well under 30 m wide) is ~30-40 m N behind a band of cottonwoods/brush and the rock ledge where the creek enters the natural bridge - not open ground. The stored evidence point (42.7347,-105.6118) is the north meadow with the picnic shelters, which is the day-use area. A creek has no view value, so a downgrade lands on 'not waterfront'. Not an --AWH value.
Pets: the county page says 'No pets are allowed in the park because of health and safety issues' - put in the note.

Unsourced stored values: max_rig_ft 30 (from Campendium via the sweep note), max_stay_nights 3 and the 'paved' sites are on no county page - left as stored, flagged. Fees $0 and the 8 sites come only from 2023-24 camper reviews; the county page gives no fee and no count.
